text: Objects are represented by functions whose output type may depend on the input, and equal represented functions determine equal objects. The required injectivity concerns this representation; it does not require each function to be injective. No assumption makes every possible function representable. Compared with [Faris §§4.1,4.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/FunLike/Basic.lean#L145).

Objects behave as functions with a fixed domain and codomain, and their values determine them uniquely. This is the constant-output-type case of the dependent interface. Individual functions may be constant or noninjective, and the interface need not represent every function between the two types. Compared with [Faris §§4.1,4.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/FunLike/Basic.lean#L157).

Each object has an underlying subset, and equal underlying subsets determine equal objects. Thus substructures with the same members are equal when this interface applies. It imposes no closure laws, finiteness, or requirement that every subset arise; those depend on the particular family of objects. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.3](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/SetLike/Basic.lean#L106).

Membership in a represented substructure means membership in its underlying subset. The implementation uses the element and substructure in that order in mathematical notation, despite the internal membership function taking the subset first. It adds no closure conditions and does not require membership to be decidable. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.3](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/SetLike/Basic.lean#L122).

For a set described by a predicate, belonging to the set means satisfying that predicate. This instance supplies the usual element-membership notation, with no search through an enumeration and no assumption that membership is decidable. It applies equally to empty, finite, and infinite sets. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.3](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/Defs.lean#L70).

This forms the type of elements belonging to a given set: an element is accompanied by evidence of its membership. It does not choose a distinguished member or assume the set is nonempty. Different proofs of the same membership do not create different mathematical elements. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.3](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Set/CoeSort.lean#L37).

Fact packages an already established proposition as an assumption that Lean can retrieve automatically. Its single field is a proof of that proposition, and unpacking it gives exactly the original claim. It supplies neither a decision procedure nor a new mathematical hypothesis beyond the proposition itself. Compared with [Aspnes §2.3](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/Logic/Basic.lean#L169).

For a type supplied with an exhaustive finite enumeration, univ is the finite set containing every element exactly once. It is empty when the type is empty. The finiteness hypothesis is essential: this construction does not provide a finite universal set for an arbitrary infinite type. Compared with [Aspnes §§3.1,3.5.5](https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/aspnes/classes/202/notes-2013.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/Fintype/Defs.lean#L92).

A submonoid is a subset containing the ambient identity and closed under multiplication. These conditions exclude the empty subset but require neither inverses nor commutativity. The interface also permits multiplication with an identity before associativity is assumed; for an ordinary monoid it gives the standard inherited submonoid. Compared with [Barr–Wells Def.2.3.10](https://abstractmath.org/CTCS/CTCS.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Submonoid/Defs.lean#L87).

Subrings contain the ambient zero and one and are closed under addition, multiplication, and negation. The shared-one convention is stronger than Judson’s possibly nonunital subrings. Mathlib also allows a zero ring and a nonassociative ambient ring; with ordinary associative rings this is precisely the usual unital subring notion. Compared with [Judson §16.1](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Subring/Defs.lean#L165).

This is a subset stable under every given scalar operation: multiplying any member by any scalar remains inside. Only the operation is assumed, so associativity and identity laws are not required here. Unlike a submodule, it needs no additive structure or zero; the empty subset is allowed. Compared with [Judson §14.1](https://judsonbooks.org/aata-files/aata-20260811.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/GroupTheory/GroupAction/SubMulAction.lean#L199).

An algebra homomorphism preserves addition, multiplication, zero, and one, and carries each base scalar’s image to the corresponding image in the target. This is the expected commuting structural-map condition. The base may be a commutative semiring, while the algebras need not be commutative or the map injective. Compared with [Schweigert Def.1.1.1,Rem.1.1.8](https://christophschweigert.github.io/skripten/a2skript.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Hom.lean#L30).

The predicate requires a nonzero semiring in which a+b=1 forces at least one summand to be a unit. For commutative rings this is equivalent to having exactly one maximal ideal. The sum formulation also makes sense without subtraction; the zero ring is explicitly excluded. Compared with [Stacks Tag00E9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00E9) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Defs.lean#L30).

Finite-dimensional means that finitely many vectors span the entire space. The scalar system may be a division ring, so commutativity is unnecessary. This concerns a finite generating family, not a finite set of all vectors: a one-dimensional real space qualifies. The zero vector space also qualifies. Compared with [Axler Def.2.9,Thm.2.31](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FiniteDimensional/Defs.lean#L74).

For a finite-dimensional vector space, finrank is its usual dimension. Generally it takes the supremum of cardinalities of linearly independent subsets, returning that natural number if finite and zero if infinite. For modules over general semirings, it need not count generators or certify finite generation. Compared with [Axler Def.2.35](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Finrank.lean#L61).

Top supplies a designated element written ⊤. By itself it assumes no order and proves no greatest-element property; that law belongs to the stronger ordered structure. This separation allows notation to be introduced before order laws, while excluding an empty carrier because an element must be supplied. Compared with [Faris §5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Notation.lean#L178).

WithTop adjoins one new point to a type, conventionally written ⊤, while retaining every original element distinctly. The new point remains separate even if the original type already had a greatest element. This definition assumes no order; interpreting the added point as greatest comes with subsequent order instances. Compared with [Faris §§4.3,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/TypeTags.lean#L22).

Extended natural numbers consist of the natural numbers, including zero, together with one additional infinity value. Every element is either finite or infinity, with those cases distinct. This is a single-point extension, not the type of all infinite cardinalities, and it does not collapse infinity to zero. Compared with [Faris §§4.3,5.1](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Data/ENat/Defs.lean#L18).

Extended nonnegative reals are the nonnegative real numbers together with a distinct infinity value, representing [0,∞]. Zero is included, while negative values and negative infinity are absent. The finite inclusion is injective and never equals infinity, matching the intended number system used for possibly infinite measures. Compared with [Faris §5.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Basic/ENNReal/Basic.lean#L104).

A complete lattice is a partially ordered set in which every subset has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound. This includes the empty subset, whose bounds are bottom and top respectively. Neither total ordering nor a restriction to countable or already bounded subsets is imposed. Compared with [Faris §5.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/CompleteLattice/Defs.lean#L142).

A subcomodule is a submodule N whose coactions land in the image of N⊗C → M⊗C. Over a field this is precisely ρ(N) ⊆ N⊗C in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Using the image makes the definition meaningful over semirings without presuming tensor inclusions injective; an inherited coaction is constructed separately under flatness. Checks pass: [coact_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L135), [mem_ofSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L172).
Stability is membership in the tensor-map range.
Construction preserves the prescribed submodule carrier.

A subcomodule is viewed as the set of vectors in its underlying submodule, consistent with the stable subspaces of [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Equality of these sets determines the submodule and its subcomodule structure, since stability is a proof property. This does not identify different embedded submodules merely because they are isomorphic. Checks pass: [mem_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L107), [ext](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L130).
Membership agrees with the stored carrier.
Equal membership predicates give equal subcomodules.

The underlying submodule ensures that a subcomodule contains zero and is closed under addition. This instance exposes precisely those existing closure properties of the stable subspaces in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Over a semiring, additive inverses are not required; closure under coaction is stored separately and is not inferred merely from additive closure. Checks pass: [mem_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L111), [rid_lTensor_coact_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L142).
Membership is the ordinary submodule membership.
Tensor contraction uses the inherited additive and scalar closure.

Scalar multiples of vectors in a subcomodule remain in that subcomodule because its carrier is an R-submodule. This supplies the expected scalar closure of [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) without choosing a basis or changing coefficients. The instance concerns scalar multiplication on vectors; it is not an additional coalgebra action or a coaction construction. Checks pass: [mem_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L111), [rid_lTensor_coact_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L142).
The carrier uses its existing submodule scalar structure.
Contraction stays in the carrier by scalar and additive closure.

This projection forgets the coaction-stability proof and returns the stored submodule, with exactly the same vectors and inclusion order. It matches the underlying stable subspace in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). It forms neither a quotient nor a space of fixed vectors, and needs no flatness because no new coaction is being lifted. Checks pass: [toSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L115), [toSubmodule_le_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L126).
Projection returns the stored carrier submodule.
Projection detects inclusion order.

Subcomodules are ordered by containment of their vectors, the usual inclusion order on stable subspaces in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Reflexivity and transitivity come from inclusion; antisymmetry holds because equal carriers determine equal subcomodules. This instance asserts only a partial order, with no assumption about tensoring preserving intersections or about arbitrary meets. Checks pass: [le_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L123), [toSubmodule_le_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L126).
Order is elementwise containment.
Underlying submodules have exactly the same order.

This constructor equips a given submodule with a proof that its coactions lie in the image of its tensored inclusion. That is the stability condition of [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), interpreted by range membership over a general semiring. It keeps the submodule unchanged and does not yet claim an inherited coaction without flatness. Checks pass: [ofSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L167), [mem_ofSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L172).
The stored carrier is exactly the input submodule.
Membership is unchanged by the constructor.

The entire module is a subcomodule: its inclusion is surjective, so every ambient coaction is in the image of its tensored inclusion. This is the full stable subspace of [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Tensoring a surjection remains surjective here; no flatness or injectivity of a general tensored submodule inclusion is needed. Checks pass: [coact_mem_tensor_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L177), [top_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L193).
Every coaction lies in the tensor image of the full submodule.
The carrier of top is the full submodule.

The zero submodule is stable because the linear coaction sends zero to zero, which has zero as a tensor preimage. It is therefore the zero subcomodule of [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Its elements are exactly zero; the construction remains valid for the zero ambient module, where the full and zero subcomodules coincide. Checks pass: [bot_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L215), [mem_bot](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L219).
Bottom has the zero submodule as its carrier.
Membership in bottom is equality to zero.

The image of a subcomodule under an intertwining linear map is again coaction-stable, as expected for the subrepresentations of [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). A tensor preimage is pushed forward through the restricted map, using the intertwining identity. This construction needs neither injectivity of the morphism nor flatness, and its carrier is the ordinary linear image. Checks pass: [map_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L294), [mem_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L307), [map_map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L346).
Carrier is the ordinary image submodule.
Image membership has an explicit source witness.
Successive images agree with the composite morphism.

Every subcomodule of a Noetherian module is finitely generated as an R-module, since its carrier is a submodule. This is the Noetherian finiteness principle discussed in [Stacks 00IJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00IJ), used here at the exact module-level hypothesis. Module.Finite means finite generation, not a finite set of vectors; flatness and a field are unnecessary. Checks pass: [toSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L115), [map_finite](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L301).
The object to which finiteness applies is the carrier submodule.
The resulting module finiteness is preserved under image maps.

Contracting the coalgebra factor of a vector’s coaction by any linear functional leaves a subcomodule invariant. A tensor preimage in N⊗C contracts to a sum of scalar multiples of vectors in N. This follows from the stability notion in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); invariance under only base-field points is not used as a converse criterion. Checks pass: [coact_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L135), [tensorComponent_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Basic.lean#L61).
Stability supplies the tensor preimage.
Each pure-tensor contraction is a scalar multiple in the carrier.

If maps preserve every subcomodule and carry any nonzero vector to any other, every nonzero subcomodule is the whole module. The supplied nonzero vector ensures bottom differs from top, matching the nonzero requirement in [Milne Definition 4.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). The family need not be a group action: preservation and the stated transitivity suffice for the argument. Checks pass: [ne_bot_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L248), [toSubmodule_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L234).
A nonzero subcomodule contains a nonzero vector.
Fullness of the underlying submodule detects the full subcomodule.

A stable submodule inherits a right coaction when C is flat: its tensored inclusion is injective, so the ambient coaction lifts uniquely. Coassociativity and the counit law then follow by inclusion into the ambient tensor products. This extends the field construction in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with flatness used as in [Stacks 00H9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). Checks pass: [induced_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L208), [subtype_rTensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L214).
The inherited coaction is the specified unique lift.
Including that coaction recovers the ambient coaction.

This map lifts the ambient coaction from N to N⊗C. Stability supplies existence of each preimage, while flatness of C makes the tensored inclusion injective and hence the lift unique and linear. Thus it implements restriction from [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with the tensor-injectivity mechanism of [Stacks 00H9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9); arbitrary preimage choices do not affect it. Checks pass: [subtype_rTensor_inducedCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L80), [subtype_rTensor_comp_inducedCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L89).
Lifted coaction maps back to the ambient coaction.
The lifting identity also holds as equality of linear maps.

With the inherited coaction, inclusion of a subcomodule is a comodule morphism: including its coaction gives the ambient one. Its underlying function is the actual subtype inclusion, so it is injective. The field picture in [Milne §4.a, p.84](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) extends here using flatness of C to construct that inherited coaction, rather than assuming all tensor inclusions injective. Checks pass: [subtype_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L235), [subtype_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L240), [subtype_rTensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L214).
The underlying linear map is the inclusion.
The morphism acts by subtype coercion.
Inclusion intertwines the inherited and ambient coactions.
